open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list configuration reread
open_points.text: “Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ, or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it” versus “the checks and the read use that one opened file”
open_points.question: When checking for a changed configuration, must the digest comparison and parsing of the replacement token list use bytes from one component-walk, one opened final file and one read, or must the kernel open and read the path a second time after detecting a change; if the path changes between those reads, which file governs the request?
options: Use one opened file and one byte snapshot for both comparison and parsing
After detecting change, repeat the component walk and parse the second opened file
Repeat the read on the same open file descriptor
open_points.default_guess: Use one component walk and one opened-file byte snapshot for both the digest comparison and parsing.

open_points.subject: installation configuration and credential final-component open
open_points.text: “each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW` … each directory on the way opened with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY` … and the last component for reading”
open_points.question: Which exact flags and procedure open the last component before it is known to be a regular file, particularly whether `O_NONBLOCK` is required so a FIFO or device is refused without blocking or causing device-specific effects?
options: Open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, then check the opened object
Open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW`, accepting that opening a non-regular object may block or have effects
First open with `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW`, check it, then obtain a separate readable descriptor
open_points.default_guess: Open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, then check and read that same descriptor.

open_points.subject: installation path-walk descriptor lifecycle
open_points.text: “each directory on the way opened with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY`, and the last component for reading”
open_points.question: When must the directory and final-file descriptors be closed, and must every descriptor be opened close-on-exec so configuration, token, or credential descriptors cannot leak into the sandbox or another child process?
options: Set `O_CLOEXEC` on every descriptor and close all path-walk descriptors after the read
Rely on runtime close-on-exec defaults and close descriptors after the read
Retain directory descriptors for later reads and define their inheritance policy
open_points.default_guess: Open every descriptor with `O_CLOEXEC` and close all of them immediately after the checked read completes.
